key_insight: In turbulent concentric annular pipe flow, wall curvature and radius ratio strongly shape passive heat transfer, so a simple linear near-wall temperature model is not sufficient.
engineering_relevance: Design and heat-transfer correlations for annular ducts should include radius-ratio effects, even at high Reynolds numbers and low Prandtl numbers, to avoid systematic prediction error.
method: Used stochastic one-dimensional turbulence (ODT) to resolve viscous, conductive, and turbulent advective transport along a radial coordinate.
Studied a wide parametric range of concentric annular pipe flow with fixed calibration at Pr = 0.71 and 0.025.
Derived boundary-layer-based logarithmic wall laws and extended Nusselt correlations to include curvature effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical predictions across an extended parameter range, showing that inner-wall boundary layers produce log-law behavior and that fitted analytical profiles match the simulation trends used to build heat-transfer scalings.
watch_item: The model calibration is fixed for only moderate and low Prandtl numbers, so applicability beyond that regime or to strongly different geometries may require revalidation.
paper_title: Numerical Simulation of Turbulent Concentric Annular Pipe Flow using One-Dimensional Turbulence (ODT): Part 2: Heat Transfer
